heading: Surgical Oncology
content:
Surgical Oncology

The Department of Surgical Oncology at ILS Hospitals employs innovative surgical procedures to deliver a holistic and patient-centred approach to cancer therapy. Our team of expert surgical oncologists is equipped with knowledge and cutting-edge technology to treat various categories of tumors. Owing to the uniqueness of each cancer type, we develop personalized treatment plans for our patients to ensure their health, well-being and long-term recovery.

Our department specialises in tumour removal with the sole aim of achieving the best possible results. Our highly skilled surgeons utilise minimally invasive techniques, such as laparoscopic surgery and robotic-assisted surgery, which reduce recovery time and minimise scarring, thereby enhancing patient comfort.

Our services :

The team provides a wide range of innovative cancer treatment options. The primary services offered are as follows :

  1. Cancer diagnosis and staging: This involves a series of comprehensive diagnostic techniques, including CT scans, MRIs, and PET scans, alongside biopsy and pathological exams, to accurately diagnose and stage cancer.
  2. Minimally invasive surgery: It mainly involves two categories:
  3. Laparoscopic surgery –  Our surgeons make use of minimally invasive techniques for various cancers, allowing for smaller incisions, quicker recovery and reduced scarring.
  4. Robotic-assisted surgery: We use state-of-the-art robotic technology for precision and minimal disruption to surrounding tissues.
  5. Tumor resection: This covers cancers of the gastrointestinal tract, lung, liver, breast, etc., where surgical removal is necessary. Radical surgery is performed in severe situations to remove all forms of malignant growth.
  6. Breast cancer surgery: Based on the patient’s condition, our surgeons perform either mastectomy (removal of the breast) or lumpectomy (removal of the tumor), in addition to sentinel lymph node biopsy and axillary dissection for staging of breast cancer.
  7. Colorectal cancer surgery: Our surgeons remove the tumor from the colon and rectum. The colorectal surgery is less invasive as it allows for faster recovery and fewer complications after surgery.
  8. Head and neck cancer surgery: Complex surgeries are performed for cancer of the mouth, throat, larynx and neck. This is followed by reconstructive surgery to restore functionality and appearance after tumor removal.
  9. Lung cancer surgery: The surgeons perform lobectomy for the removal of lung tumors along with mediastinal lymph node dissection for accurate staging.
  10. Gastrointestinal cancer surgery: Surgeons use this method to treat cancers of the stomach, liver, pancreas, and esophagus.
  11. Endocrine cancer surgery: This method is preferred for endocrine malignancies, including those of the thyroid, parathyroid, and adrenal glands.
  12. Reconstructive surgery: This involves post-surgical reconstructive procedures, especially for breast, head and neck cancers, to restore function as well as appearance.
  13. Palliative surgery: Surgeons make use of certain techniques to ease symptoms and improve the quality of life for individuals with advanced stages of cancer.

title: Medical Oncology
heading: Medical Oncology
content:
Medical Oncology

Through our comprehensive Medical Oncology program at ILS Hospitals, we focus on providing personalized care to cancer patients. Using cutting-edge technologies, our department specializes in detecting and treating cancer at all stages, from early to advanced. Every year, our highly qualified oncologists treat hundreds of patients with various types of cancer and advise them on the best course of treatment for their specific needs.

Our oncologists are experts in managing drug therapies for cancers affecting various organs, muscles, bones, and connective tissue. Although early-stage cancer can sometimes be treated with surgery or radiation alone, many patients need the help of an oncologist in complex cases, who are experts in identifying and treating a wide range of cancerous conditions, including breast, lung, colon, pancreatic prostate, ovarian, and other gynecological cancers; liver and biliary cancers; brain tumors; head and neck cancers among others.

Our patients benefit from access to both conventional and experimental therapies. We collaborate closely with professionals from other specialities to create a comprehensive, integrated treatment plan, which enables us to provide the best potential outcomes for patients, increasing their chances of healing, survival, and a higher quality of life. Since its inception, ILS hospitals have been at the forefront of cancer care, and we continue to be a trusted choice for people seeking expert, compassionate treatment for cancer.

Our Services

Our medical oncology services cover a broad spectrum of therapies, including:

  1. Chemotherapy: Chemotherapy is used to treat a wide variety of cancers, with the most effective medications tailored to each patient’s specific type and stage. Patients undergoing treatment benefit from outpatient chemotherapy services, which ensure their comfort and convenience.
  2. Targeted Therapy: Precision medicine focuses on specific molecular and genetic abnormalities found in cancer cells. These medications target cancer cell growth mechanisms while minimizing harm to healthy cells, resulting in more effective treatments with fewer side effects.
  3. Immunotherapy: We provide checkpoint inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and CAR-T cell therapy for a wide range of cancers, including those that are resistant to traditional treatments.
  4. Hormone Therapy: Cancers such as breast and prostate cancer are hormone-sensitive cancers that are treated by blocking or reducing hormone levels that accelerate tumor growth. This is done by providing endocrine therapies such as aromatase inhibitors and selective estrogen receptor modulators.
  5. Personalized Cancer Treatment Plans: The treatment plans are tailored to the cancer’s specific type and molecular characteristics. Our team of oncologists, pathologists, and radiologists ensures that each patient receives a thorough, personalized treatment plan.
  6. Cancer Screening and Early Detection: This involves providing comprehensive screening services to detect cancers at an initial and more treatable stage. Advanced diagnostic tools, including blood tests, imaging, and genetic testing, are utilised to enhance detection and prevention.
  7. Palliative Care: Supportive care is provided to cancer patients to alleviate symptoms, reduce pain, and improve quality of life. Chemotherapy is offered to relieve pain while maintaining a focus on the patient’s overall health.
  8. Bone Marrow Transplantation: We provide stem cell and bone marrow transplants for certain types of cancers, such as leukemia and lymphoma , in order to restore healthy blood cells and improve patient outcomes.

title: Radiation Oncology
heading: Radiation Oncology
content:
Radiation Oncology

Radiation oncologists at ILS hospital treat a broad range of malignancies annually, tailoring state-of-the-art care to each patient’s specific needs. Our centre is renowned for delivering high-quality radiation therapy by combining advanced equipment with the extensive experience of our medical personnel. Our radiation oncologists are highly skilled in employing cutting-edge technologies to treat a wide spectrum of cancers, ensuring that each patient receives the best possible care. We take great care to focus radiation on malignant tumors, limiting the harm to healthy tissues and organs while increasing the effectiveness of the treatment.

The department offers care for a range of cancer types through disease-specific teams. These teams assess and treat patients with complicated cancer diagnoses by combining the knowledge of experts from different medical specialities. Each expert team collaborates closely to create individualized treatment plans to ensure that the patient receives the most appropriate and efficient care possible. We are dedicated to assisting you throughout your cancer journey, regardless of whether you are being treated for a common or complex malignancy.

Our Services :

  • External Beam Radiation Therapy (EBRT): We use this noninvasive radiation therapy, in which a high-energy beam is administered to the target tumor site from outside the body. EBRT is used to treat breast, prostate, lung, and brain cancers.
  • Brachytherapy (Internal Radiation Therapy): We use a radioactive material which is placed inside or close to the tumor cells or tissues. It is most widely recommended to treat prostate, cervical cancer, and several head and neck-related malignancies.
  • Radiation Therapy: We use high-dose radiation that is administered directly to the tumor cells, with little or no exposure to neighbouring healthy cells.
  • Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS): This is a non-surgical radiation technique used at ILS hospital in which a precise dose of radiation is delivered to the targeted area. It is commonly used against brain tumors and malformations in the blood vessels, with negligible damage to the adjacent tissues.
  • Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT): This is a cutting-edge form of radiation therapy used at ILS hospitals in which extremely focused beams of radiation are delivered to cancerous cells. It is recommended for the treatment of tumors in the lungs, liver, spine, and pancreas, especially when surgery is not recommended.
  • Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy (IMRT): It is an advanced procedure used at our hospital in which computer-controlled linear accelerators deliver a controlled quantity of radiation to tumor cells. It helps radiation oncologists treat complex tumors with minimum exposure to healthy tissues. This procedure is ideal for head and neck cancers, prostate cancer, and others.
  • Image-Guided Radiation Therapy (IGRT): Our experts use modern imaging techniques (such as CT scans or MRIs) to perform the radiation treatment with greater accuracy. IGRT permits the radiation oncologist to adjust the position of the radiation beam based on real-time images, which improves accuracy and minimizes the risk of damaging healthy tissues.
  • Proton Therapy: Here, we use protons in place of X-rays. In this form of therapy, our Oncologists target a highly precise amount of protons with minimal radiation exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. It is effectively used in the treatment of cancers related to the pediatric population, brain tumors, and cancers near vital organs.
  • Radiosensitization: Certain drugs or therapies make cancer cells more sensitive to radiation. These drugs may be used in combination with radiation therapy to improve their efficacy, especially against tumors that show resistance to conventional treatments.
  • Palliative Radiation Therapy: It is utilized to reduce symptoms of advanced cancer, like pain, bleeding, or breathlessness, without the treatment of the disease. It is frequently recommended to treat conditions like bone tumor, tumors of the brain and those obstructing the airways.
  • Radiation Therapy for Non-Cancerous Conditions: We utilise this procedure to treat various non-cancerous conditions, including thyroid eye disease and vascular malformations. It is also used to shrink abnormal cell growth or for pain management in non-malignant conditions.

title: Pediatric Oncology
heading: Pediatric Oncology
content:
Pediatric Oncology

ILS hospitals recognizes that a pediatric cancer diagnosis is a difficult and emotional experience for both children and their families. Our specialized staff is committed to delivering complete care right from diagnosis to treatment, survivorship, and beyond. Our team of experts prioritize the requirements of each child by focusing on their medical and emotional status and offers patient-centred therapy and care. We employ a collaborative approach to deliver essential support for physical recovery and emotional well-being.

A few of them are listed  as follows:

  • Comprehensive, coordinated care: Our pediatric cancer department employs a collaborative approach, ensuring that all services, from diagnostics to treatment and follow-up, are seamlessly integrated into a single, comprehensive procedure. We emphasize accurate diagnosis and swift treatment, which helps to minimize delays and ensure that your child receives prompt care. Our pediatric cancer specialists collaborate with child life experts and various medical professionals to deliver optimal treatment while addressing the emotional needs of children and their families.
  • Expert pediatric cancer specialists: Our pediatric oncologists have extensive experience treating a wide range of childhood cancers, including those that are particularly challenging to treat. Our care team consists of board-certified pediatric doctors who collaborate to ensure that each child receives the best available treatment.
  • Lymphoma and Leukemia Care: Our doctors have vast experience in diagnosing and treating different kinds of leukemias and lymphomas. Our team collaborates with pathologists and other experts to ensure correct diagnosis and that each patient gets the best treatment.
  • Treatment for sarcoma: Pediatric oncologists collaborate with experts from other specialities on a multidisciplinary sarcoma program. From the first meeting, this team collaborates to determine the most effective way to treat children with complex sarcomas.
  • Brain tumor care: Pediatric neurologists, oncologists, and neurosurgeons provide skilled care for children with brain tumors. Our team of experts ensures that surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, and other treatments are done promptly to improve outcomes.
  • Proton Beam treatment: If your child has complex or pediatric cancer, we help them with cutting-edge proton beam treatment, a very accurate type of radiation therapy. This treatment has negligible side effects on healthy cells, which helps preserve fertility for future health.
  • Bone Marrow Transplant: Our bone marrow transplant program is one of the largest in the country. Pediatric experts from various fields collaborate to make individualized transplant plans and offer ongoing support while the child recovers.

Cancer treatment for pediatric patients requires a specialized strategy that considers issues including sexuality, social networks, and mental well-being. This age group has unique healthcare requirements, and our program is designed to address those needs.  We are dedicated to delivering comprehensive, compassionate pediatric cancer care that caters to the emotional and medical requirements of children and their families during their cancer journey.

Hemato Oncology

The Hematology Oncology department at ILS hospitals provides specialist care to patients suffering from blood cancers. Our core specialists, highly skilled in the diagnosis, treatment, and management of various blood cancers, are equipped with the latest technology to ensure proper operation and optimal outcomes for patients. title: Preventive Oncology
heading: Preventive Oncology
content:
Preventive Oncology

Cancer is preventable. The good news is that we, at ILS hospital, have the expertise to reduce the risk of developing cancer by making key lifestyle changes. It is estimated that nearly half of all cancer cases either result from modifiable risk factors or can be detected in their early stages before they develop. By adopting a healthier lifestyle, such as maintaining a balanced diet, staying physically active, managing a healthy weight, and avoiding tobacco use, we can significantly lower our chances of developing cancer. Alongside preventive measures, early detection remains one of the most effective ways to combat cancer.

Our Services

Our department of Preventive Oncology provides a variety of services to help people minimize their cancer risk and detect potential malignant alterations early. These services include the following:

  • Health education: Providing information on cancer prevention and the importance of early detection.
  • Cancer risk assessment: Helping individuals understand their cancer risk factors.
  • Encouraging active health management: Promoting regular cancer screenings and empowering individuals to track their health.
  • Specialized services: Offering behaviour counselling and diet planning for cancer prevention.

Our team of consultants, counsellors, dietitians, and health professionals collaborates to deliver high-quality services to our community. We provide health education materials covering cancer prevention, self-exams, clinical examinations, and appropriate screenings.

Cancer Warning Symptoms – CAUTION

While you take proactive steps toward staying cancer-free, it is important to remain alert to any potential warning signs of cancer, including:

  • Changes in bowel or bladder habits
  • A sore that doesn’t heal
  • Unusual bleeding or discharge
  • Thickening or lumps in the breast or any part of the body
  • Indigestion or difficulty swallowing
  • Obvious changes in a wart or mole
  • Persistent cough or hoarseness

While these symptoms do not always signal cancer, it is critical to see a doctor if you have any of them. Screening tests are useful even if you don’t have symptoms since they can uncover potential problems before they worsen. Early detection enables earlier treatment, which can considerably improve outcomes. At ILS hospital, we are dedicated to helping you take control of your health and reduce your risk of cancer through education, screening, and expert care.

title: Bone Marrow Transplant
heading: Bone Marrow Transplant
content:
Bone Marrow Transplant

The Bone Marrow and Stem Cell Transplant department at ILS hospitals is known for its expertise in the treatment of blood and bone marrow-related disorders such as leukemia, bone marrow failure syndromes, and multiple myeloma, among others. Our experts are highly skilled in managing rare blood diseases and offer a range of transplantation options, including autologous (self-donor) and allogeneic (donor) stem cell transplants. Our mandate is to provide comprehensive treatment and management of all bone marrow and blood disorders under one roof, aiming to improve patients’ overall outcomes and quality of life.

The Bone Marrow Transplantation team works closely with specialists in hematology, oncology, immunology, and other areas to develop a personalized treatment plan for our patients. We also offer access to clinical trials for experimental treatments, giving patients the opportunity to explore new therapies that may benefit their condition.

Our Services

  • Allogeneic stem cell transplantation: This treatment involves replacing damaged bone marrow with stem cells from a matched donor.
  • Autologous stem cell transplantation: Following high-dose chemotherapy, we typically provide patients with stem cells to restore healthy bone marrow function.
  • Cell therapy and on-site stem cell processing: This is a cutting-edge therapy that manipulates stem cells to increase their effectiveness in treating diseases.
  • Conditioning: Pre-transplant chemotherapy or radiation therapy is used to prepare the body for stem cell infusions.
  • Cord blood transplantation: This therapeutic method utilises stem cells derived from umbilical cord blood and is suitable for individuals without an available adult donor.
  • Myeloablative conditioning: High-dose chemotherapy or radiation is used to destroy abnormal bone marrow prior to transplantation.
  • Outpatient transplantation: In some cases, patients may be able to receive stem cell transplants as outpatients, avoiding the need for extended hospital stays.
  • Reduced-intensity conditioning: This is a less aggressive pre-transplant regimen for patients who cannot tolerate traditional myeloablative therapy.
  • Pediatric transplantation: It is specialized care for children, with an emphasis on minimizing long-term consequences and promoting growth and development.
  • Treatment for rare disorders: We also offer stem cell transplants to patients with rare conditions such as amyloidosis, which require specialized care.

title: Immunotherapy
heading: Immunotherapy
content:
Immunotherapy

Immunotherapy is the process of activating the body’s defence mechanisms to combat cancer. Here at ILS hospitals, this procedure has delivered promising results for patients with various types of cancer, especially those that are difficult to treat with chemotherapy and radiation.

Our services include a wide range of options tailored to the specific needs of the patient to boost the body’s immune system. Our experts closely monitor patients’ conditions and suggest treatment plans best suited to their needs. This method has been proven to improve outcomes for patients who have not responded well to routine treatments. It helps to improve survival and recovery. Our primary goal is to deliver the most effective treatment to enhance the health of our patients.

Our Services

  • Monoclonal antibody therapy: We use lab-made antibodies to target cancer cells, which assist the immune system in destroying them.
  • Checkpoint inhibitors: They help the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells. This process is undertaken for melanoma and lung cancer.
  • CAR T-cell therapy: This therapy uses the body’s immune cells to fight cancer. It is particularly effective for Blood cancer.
  • Cytokine therapy: We use certain medications that stimulate the immune system to fight cancer effectively, which helps to fight cancer of the kidney, melanoma and leukemia/blood cancer.
  • Cancer vaccines: We administer these vaccines to stimulate the immune system to attack cancer cells. They are effective in treating Cervical Cancer.
  • Oncolytic virus therapy: We use genetically modified viruses that stimulate an immune response that targets and destroys specific cancer cells.
  • Immune checkpoint blockade: This method blocks certain proteins that inhibit the functioning of the immune system.
  • Adaptive T-cell transfer: We extract specific immune cells from your blood, modify them in the lab, and reintroduce them to boost the body’s immune response to cancer.
  • Tumor-infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) therapy: We isolate immune cells from the tumor, culture them in the laboratory, and reintroduce them to combat cancer effectively. This therapy is useful in treating melanoma.
  • Immune modulators: These are drugs that modify the immune system’s function to enhance its ability to fight cancer. They are particularly effective in treating multiple myeloma.

heading: Oncopathology
content:
Oncopathology

Oncopathology at ILS hospitals is a specialized approach to the management and treatment of cancer. It involves treating various blood-related disorders that occur due to cancer or its treatment, such as anaemia. Through our advanced oncopathology services, we offer state-of-the-art care to manage these complications. Our experts collaborate closely with other departments to deliver high-quality care to cancer patients.

Our focus is on diagnosing and treating the side effects of cancer therapy. Blood and platelet transfusions, along with the administration of growth factors to boost blood cell production, help patients maintain their strength and immune system during cancer treatment. Our oncology services are designed to ensure that cancer patients not only fight cancer but also manage the complexities that come with their treatment, leading to better outcomes and an improved quality of life.

Our  Services  are  essential for :

  • Accurate cancer diagnosis – We help patients differentiate between non-cancerous and cancerous tumors.
  • Cancer staging and grading: We use the latest technology to determine the extent and rate of cancer’s spread in the body.
  • Treatment planning – We assist oncologists in selecting the most effective therapies for targeted treatments.
  • Monitoring treatment response – We evaluate whether a patient’s cancer is responding to a particular therapy.
  • Detecting recurrences – We identify cancer that has a chance of returning after treatment and adjust the treatment plan accordingly.

title: Medical Genetics
heading: Medical Genetics
content:
Medical Genetics

At the Medical Genetics department of ILS Hospitals, advanced genomic testing is used to personalize healthcare. We provide novel approaches to planning, preventing, diagnosing, and treating various medical problems. Our team uses your DNA to create treatment plans tailored to your genetic profile, taking a more individualized approach to medical treatment.

Our medical genetics department offers a comprehensive array of services, including family history assessments and whole genome sequencing to diagnose rare genetic illnesses. By examining the genetic code at the molecular level, we assist our patients in gaining a comprehensive understanding of their health issues so they may take an active approach to their therapy.

Medical geneticists, licensed genetic counsellors, and skilful nurses make an integral part of our team, who collaborate to deliver accurate genetic evaluations and individualized care plans. We interact with other specialists as needed to provide a comprehensive approach to patient care. Whether you have a known genetic disease or are unsure about your family’s health history, our staff provide the expertise and guidance you require. These services are especially valuable to people who have been adopted or have limited information about their family’s health history. We help you determine a genetic condition and offer advice on the next steps in care.

Our Services

  • Our licensed genetic counsellors are experts in medical genetics and counselling. They help patients review their family medical history, personal health concerns, and symptoms related to genetic conditions. Our team will educate you on different genetic testing choices. Whether you’re concerned about cancer risks, neurological issues, heart disease, developmental delays, or uncommon genetic diseases, our counsellors will walk you through the entire procedure. Topics commonly discussed with genetic counsellors include:
  • Your genetic risk is based on family history or personal health history.

title: Nuclear Medicine
heading: Nuclear Medicine
content:
Nuclear Medicine

We use a comprehensive and multidisciplinary approach to nuclear medicine therapy, bringing together professionals from several departments to create personalized treatment programs for each patient who visits ILS hospitals. Our mission is to deliver the most effective and personalised care to every patient.

Nuclear medicine therapy involves the use of radioactive medications that selectively target cancer cells. These medications attach to cancerous cells on intravenous administration and eliminate them through radiation. Over time, the body eliminates toxic waste through urine, although some of it can also pass through the bloodstream. It is mostly used to treat patients who show resistance to chemotherapy or surgery. Although it might not completely remove the cancer, treatment can manage symptoms, reduce tumor size, and stabilize the condition, often for long periods. To achieve the best outcomes, nuclear medicine therapy is typically used in conjunction with other medications.

Our Services

Diagnostic imaging

  • PET scan: This sensitive imaging technique is used to diagnose various types of cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and neurological disorders. It provides detailed images related to several metabolic activities.
  • SPECT scan: This procedure uses imaging to visualise organs, such as the heart, brain, and bones, to detect cancer, neurological disorders, and cardiovascular diseases.
  • Thyroid Scintigraphy: This procedure is used to assess thyroid function and diagnose thyroid disorders, including cancer.
  • Bone Scintigraphy: It is a procedure for detecting bone tumors, infections, or fractures by emphasizing locations with aberrant bone activity.
  • Renal Scintigraphy: It is used to assess kidney function and diagnose kidney-related diseases.

Therapeutic Nuclear Medicine

  • Radioactive Iodine Therapy (RAI): The method is used to treat hyperthyroidism and thyroid cancer that targets and kills malignant thyroid cells using radioactive iodine.
  • PRRT: It is a targeted therapy for tumors of the nervous and endocrine systems that uses certain compounds to deliver radiation to cancer cells.
  • Radium Therapy: It treats prostate cancer that has progressed to the bones by providing targeted radiation to cancer cells in bone tissue.

Radioactive Seed Implantation:

It is a type of internal radiation therapy that is frequently used to treat prostate cancer and involves implanting tiny radioactive seeds into or close to the tumor site.

Cardiac Muclear Medicine

  • Myocardial Perfusion Imaging (MPI): It is a non-invasive test that measures blood flow in the heart muscle to identify coronary artery disease and assess heart function.
  • Cardiac Stress Test: This test utilises nuclear medicine to evaluate heart function under stress, identifying potential blockages in coronary arteries or other cardiac conditions.

Lung scintigraphy:

This ventilation/Perfusion (V/Q) scan evaluates blood and airflow in the lungs to help diagnose lung conditions such as pulmonary embolism.

Liver and spleen imaging

  • HIDA Scan: This test evaluates liver, gallbladder, and bile duct function, aiding in the diagnosis of conditions such as gallstones, inflammation, and bile duct blockage.
  • Spleen Scintigraphy: This technique evaluates spleen function and detects abnormalities, such as spleen enlargement.

Gastrointestinal imaging

  • Gastric Emptying Studies: These tests determine how well food moves from the stomach to the small intestine, which aids in the diagnosis of various underlying conditions.
  • Liver & Pancreatic Scintigraphy: It is used to evaluate pancreatic function and diagnose diseases such as pancreatic cancer or pancreatitis.

Infection and inflammation imaging:

White Blood Cell (WBC) scintigraphy: This approach detects infections by monitoring the activity of white blood cells (WBCs), which can help locate hidden infections, abscesses, or inflammation in the body.

Neuroendocrine tumor imaging

Somatostatin Receptor Scintigraphy (SRS): Imaging somatostatin receptors is used to detect tumors of the nervous and endocrine system, which can help spot cancers that are difficult to detect using typical imaging methods.

Preparation for surgery and treatment planning

Tumor Localization: Nuclear medicine techniques are used to identify cancers prior to surgery or radiation therapy, allowing surgeons to undertake more precise tumor resections and treatment plans

title: Blood Bank
heading: Blood Bank
content:
Blood Bank

ILS hospitals offer life-saving support to cancer patients recovering from chemotherapy, which results in blood cell depletion. Our blood bank is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities to ensure vital transfusions for patients’ survival. All standard precautions are undertaken to ensure that every blood product is safe and effective for use.
Patients undergoing chemotherapy require regular blood transfusions. Our blood bank ensures an uninterrupted supply of pure and healthy blood, plasma, and platelets, depending on the specific needs of cancer patients.
Our experienced staff works with the blood bank to ensure timely and appropriate transfusions, minimize complications, and enhance the patient’s response to treatment. Screening tests are carried out on the blood samples to ensure safety during administration.

Services We Offer:

Blood Transfusion Services

  • Red Blood Cell (RBC) transfusions: We offer these to patients with anemia caused by cancer treatments, like chemotherapy or radiation. They help increase oxygen delivery to tissues and improve overall energy levels.
  • Platelet transfusions: These are provided to patients with low platelet counts, a common side effect of chemotherapy, to prevent bleeding and manage clotting disorders.
  • Fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) transfusions: We treat patients with clotting problems or bleeding disorders resulting from cancer or its treatment.
  • Stem cell and bone marrow Support: Our blood bank supports stem cell and bone marrow transplants by providing compatible blood products and maintaining careful matching procedures, all while ensuring the safety and efficacy of transplants.
  • Cross-matching and compatibility testing: We perform these procedures to ensure that blood products are compatible with the patient’s immune system. This is especially crucial for individuals who may require frequent blood transfusions during their treatment.
  • Blood product screening: We screen blood products for infectious diseases. Cancer patients with compromised immune systems rely on safe, screened blood products.
  • Autologous blood donation: Patients can donate their blood before undergoing treatment (such as chemotherapy or surgery). This blood is stored and later used for transfusions during or after treatment, reducing the risk of complications associated with donor blood.
  • Support for stem cell transplantation: Our blood bank provides the necessary blood components during and after stem cell transplants for hematologic cancers. It ensures an adequate blood supply to manage side effects and promote recovery.
  • Emergency blood supply: In cases of acute blood loss or severe complications during cancer treatments, our blood bank ensures an emergency supply of blood products to address the patient’s immediate needs.

title: Pain and Palliative Care
heading: Pain and Palliative Care
content:
Pain and Palliative Care

Our oncology department at ILS hospitals is dedicated to providing comprehensive care for cancer patients, with a special focus on pain management and enhancing the quality of life. In addition to addressing physical discomfort, we offer extensive support for the patient’s emotional, psychological, and spiritual needs.

The main focus of our pain and palliative care oncology department is to provide comprehensive care for cancer patients, alongside pain management. This way, we address the physical discomforts caused by cancer and its treatments and offer emotional, psychological, and spiritual support to patients and their families.
We also offer medications, nerve blocks, and radiation therapy for pain relief. Our specialists tailor treatment plans based on individual needs, ensuring maximum comfort.

Emphasis is placed on symptom control, addressing issues such as nausea, fatigue, and breathing difficulties. We also support patients’ emotional well-being through counselling. Our team collaborates with oncologists to ensure that patients receive comprehensive care that enhances their overall quality of life throughout their cancer journey.

Our Services:

  • Pain management: We use medications and physical therapy to relieve pain caused by surgery or treatment side effects.
  • Symptom control: We address issues like nausea, shortness of breath, fatigue, loss of appetite, anxiety, and sleep disturbances through involved medications, counselling, dietary changes, and alternative therapies.
  • Emotional and psychological support: We have provisions for counselling and mental health services to help patients and families cope with fear, depression, or anxiety.
  • Spiritual and social support: Our program helps patients find meaning and purpose in their journey, guided by spiritual advisors. The social workers assist with financial concerns, insurance, and care planning.
  • End-of-life care (Hospice care): This is specifically for individuals who are in the final stages of a terminal illness. Our team focuses on comfort rather than curing the disease.
